Tariffs on EVs under Section 301 will rise from 25% to 100% in 2024.
Tariffs on lithium-ion EV batteries will rise from 7.5% to 25% in 2024
Effective from 1 November 2025, the US government has imposed 25% tariffs on imported medium and heavy-duty vehicles (Classes 3-8) and 25% on many of their parts.
Hyundai is expanding its US output, boosting capacity in Georgia, and has adjusted its operating profit margin targets downward to account for tariff pressures.
Natural graphite will face tariffs of 25%, as will permanent magnets, starting 2026.
Nissan announced that it will drop the 2026 Ariya electric SUV from its US. lineup. One of the reasons cited is the 15% tariff imposed on Japanese-built EVs under the US–Japan trade framework.
Permanent magnets will draw a tariff of 25% from 2026 onwards.
Starting this year the US is increasing the tariff rate on lithium ion batteries and battery parts to 25% from 7.5% earlier.

For non-electric vehicle lithium ion batteries a tariff of 25% will be introduced in 2026.
